title: Build Performance, Dynamic Features, and Library Modules Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best demonstrates sound build performance, dynamic features, and library modules?
options: Measure an incremental build scenario, assess whether statements should be a normal or dynamic feature, and define the public surface of a reusable banking SDK module.
Claiming modularisation improved build speed after comparing one clean build on different machine conditions.
Copy the largest sample architecture without measuring its fit
Hide dependencies behind global lookup to reduce constructor parameters
questions.answer: Measure an incremental build scenario, assess whether statements should be a normal or dynamic feature, and define the public surface of a reusable banking SDK module.
questions.explanation: The sound choice names the protected contract and requires observable evidence rather than structural appearance.

questions.prompt: Adding more interfaces and Gradle modules always improves application architecture.
questions.explanation: Every boundary has cost and must protect a real responsibility, change seam, ownership rule, or measured build property.

questions.prompt: What evidence should accompany the build performance, dynamic features, and library modules decision?
questions.answer: A focused behavioural test, dependency graph rule, failure scenario, or measurement tied to the claimed benefit.
questions.explanation: Architecture claims become reviewable when a specific check can prove or disprove them.
